EOSC 110.title: The Solid Earth: A Dynamic Planet
EOSC 110.description: Earth's origin, composition, structure, and natural resources. Plate tectonics as the driving force for volcanism, mountain building, and earthquakes. Imaging Earth's interior. Environmental geoscience and sustainability. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list for the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.)

EOSC 111.title: Laboratory Exploration of Planet Earth
EOSC 111.description: An examination of the processes that shape and change the planet earth. This laboratory course is an appropriate complement to EOSC 110, EOSC 112, EOSC 114, EOSC 116 but can also be taken independently.

EOSC 112.title: The Climate System
EOSC 112.description: Introduction to Earth's climate system: radiation balance, greenhouse effect, atmosphere and ocean circulation, plate tectonics, biosphere interactions, and the carbon cycle. Applications to understand the causes of climate change, from long-term climate evolution to modern human-induced climate change. (Consult the Credit Exclusion list, within the Faculty of Science section in the Calendar.)

EOSC 114.title: The Catastrophic Earth: Natural Disasters
EOSC 114.description: Introduction to causes and physical characteristics of disasters such as volcanic eruptions, earthquakes, tsunamis, hurricanes, storm surge, thunderstorms, tornadoes, landslides, wind waves, meteor impacts, mass extinctions.

EOSC 116.title: Mesozoic Earth: Time of the Dinosaurs.
EOSC 116.description: Earth's tectonics, climate, and oceans during the time of the dinosaurs. Reading the fossil record of Earth from its earliest origins up to and including the Mesozoic, 250 - 65 million years ago.

EOSC 118.title: Earth's Treasures: Gold and Gems
EOSC 118.description: Origin, properties, valuation, prospecting and geology of gold, platinum, silver, diamonds, rubies, emeralds, and other precious metals and gems.

EOSC 210.title: Earth Science for Engineers
EOSC 210.description: Focus on the interaction between society and the geologic environment. Locating, assessing and developing natural resources; understanding and preparing for natural hazards, design of structures and waste disposal sites.

EOSC 211.title: Computer Methods in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences
EOSC 211.description: Mathematical computer-based problem solving in the physical, chemical, and biological sciences. Problems drawn from studies of the earth, the oceans and the atmosphere.
EOSC 211.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001

EOSC 212.title: Topics in the Earth and Planetary Sciences.
EOSC 212.description: Cutting edge problems in earth, ocean, atmospheric and planetary sciences. Topics will be introduced through discussions of the current literature.

prerequisite.raw: Second-year standing in science or engineering

EOSC 212.prerequisiteText: Second-year standing in science or engineering

EOSC 213.title: Computational Methods in Geological Engineering
EOSC 213.description: Combining basic physical principles with their mathematical description and generating computational models that describe them. Introduction to basic building blocks in modelling, simulation and parameter estimation.
EOSC 213.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 253 and one of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223 and one of APSC_V 160, CPSC_V 103, CPSC_V 110, EOSC_V 211

EOSC 220.title: Introductory Mineralogy
EOSC 220.description: Introduction to crystallography, physical and chemical properties of minerals. Recognition and identification of common minerals. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
EOSC 220.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 120, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, CHEM_V 154, SCIE_V 001

EOSC 221.title: Introductory Petrology
EOSC 221.description: Optical mineralogy and the classification and genesis of igneous, metamorphic and sedimentary rocks.

EOSC 222.title: Geological Time and Stratigraphy
EOSC 222.description: Measuring geological time and understanding Earth history using stratigraphic principles, paleontology and radioactive decay. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:
notes: One of EOSC 1**, EOSC 210, GEOB 103 is recommended.

EOSC 223.title: Field Techniques
EOSC 223.description: Introduction to the techniques of geological mapping and the interpretation of field data. Includes three one-day field trips on weekends plus a seven-day field school after Spring examinations. A fee is to be paid by January 31.

EOSC 240.title: Site Investigation
EOSC 240.description: Theory and practice of site investigation for geological engineers, including background studies, field work, remote sensing, development of ground models, importance of geological variability and uncertainty. Impacts on design, project risk and decision making.

EOSC 250.title: Fields and Fluxes
EOSC 250.description: Application of classical theory of scalar and vector fields to geophysical sciences. Conductive, convective and radiative energy flux, gravitation, electrostatics, and magnetostatics. Gauss' and Stokes' theorems.
EOSC 250.prerequisiteText: MATH_V 200 and one of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 157
notes: One of PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 158 is recommended.

EOSC 256.title: Earthquakes
EOSC 256.description: Characteristics, types, plate tectonics, faults, earth stresses and strains, seismic waves, magnitude scales, instrumentation, hazard mapping, prediction, and forecasting.
EOSC 256.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157; or (b) SCIE 001

EOSC 270.title: Marine Ecosystems
EOSC 270.description: Introduction to diversity of marine habitats and ecosystems; hydrothermal vent, intertidal, coral reef, estuarine, deep sea, and polar ecosystems; impacts of ecosystem change; evolution of ocean plankton; invasive species; climate change; pollution.
EOSC 270.prerequisiteText: One of SCIE 001, CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141, CHEM 154

EOSC 310.title: The Earth and the Solar System
EOSC 310.description: The Earth as a planet: its composition, internal dynamics, and surface evolution. Rotation, magnetic field, plate tectonics, earthquakes, volcanoes. The ocean, atmosphere, and biosphere as components of a varying geo-environment. Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( No background in science or mathematics is required. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

EOSC 311.title: The Earth and its Resources
EOSC 311.description: An introduction to the Earth with emphasis on its industrial and aesthetic resources. Rocks, minerals, gold, diamonds, sediments, fossils, oil and gas, canyons, and volcanoes and the processes that create them. Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( No background in science or mathematics is required.

EOSC 314.title: The Ocean Environment
EOSC 314.description: An introduction to the oceans and the processes that have shaped them, their composition and movement, waves, tides, beaches, interactions with the atmosphere and human exploitation of the non-living resources. Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( No background in science or mathematics is required.

EOSC 315.title: The Ocean Ecosystem
EOSC 315.description: An introduction to life in the oceans, its variety and evolution; primary producers and their links to the environment, zooplankton, marine communities, living marine resources and their role in today's world. Not for credit for students in specializations administered by the Department of Earth, Ocean, and Atmospheric Sciences. ( No background in science or mathematics is required.

EOSC 320.title: Sedimentology
EOSC 320.description: Origin, diagenesis and geochemistry of sediments and sedimentary rocks.
EOSC 320.prerequisiteText: EOSC 221 and one of EOSC 210, EOSC 222

EOSC 321.title: Igneous Petrology
EOSC 321.description: The origin and formation of igneous rocks.

EOSC 322.title: Metamorphic Petrology
EOSC 322.description: Deciphering lithospheric processes as recorded by the mineralogy, chemistry and textures of metamorphosed rocks.

EOSC 323.title: Structural Geology I
EOSC 323.description: Analysis and interpretation of natural deformation.
EOSC 323.prerequisiteText: All of EOSC 221, EOSC 223 and one of EOSC 210, EOSC 222

EOSC 325.title: Principles of Physical Hydrogeology
EOSC 325.description: Theories of storage and movement of water within groundwater systems; Groundwater-surface water interaction; Role of groundwater systems in watershed management and regulating the environmental impacts of global change; Groundwater sustainability; Impacts of climate & land use changes on groundwater resources. .

children.raw: 3rd year standing in Science, Land and Food Systems, or Forestry and Environmental Stewardship

EOSC 325.prerequisiteText: (a) 3rd year standing in Science, Land and Food Systems, or Forestry and Environmental Stewardship; and (b) One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, SCIE_V 001

EOSC 326.title: Earth and Life Through Time
EOSC 326.description: The fossil record of adaptation and extinction emphasizing the interaction of biological and geological processes. Not for credit in Geological Sciences and Geophysics specializations. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List: Second-year class standing or higher.

EOSC 327.title: Geochemical Thermodynamics
EOSC 327.description: Application of chemical thermodynamics to problem solving in the earth sciences. Geochemical tools are developed for: low-T aqueous geochemistry, high-T, high-P processes in the lithosphere, ore-deposit formation, and for prediction of geochemical reaction rates in all environments.

EOSC 328.title: Field Geology
EOSC 328.description: Recording and processing geological data in the field. Held within the three weeks following April examinations after third year. A special fee is to be paid by January 31.
EOSC 328.prerequisiteText: All of EOSC_V 323, EOSC_V 330 and one of EOSC_V 321, EOSC_V 322

EOSC 329.title: Quantitative Groundwater Hydrology
EOSC 329.description: Introduction to theory of groundwater flow; flow nets; regional groundwater resource evaluation; well hydraulics; role of groundwater in geologic processes, case studies.
EOSC 329.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121, SCIE 001

EOSC 330.title: Principles of Geomorphology
EOSC 330.description: Landform development; morphological and historical analysis of landforms; applications in engineering and resource development. Please consult the Faculty of Science Credit Exclusion List:

EOSC 331.title: Introduction to Mineral Deposits
EOSC 331.description: Introduction to economic geology and models related to mineral exploration. Study includes typical deposit types and their plate tectonic setting.

EOSC 332.title: Tectonic Evolution of North America
EOSC 332.description: An overview of the geology and tectonic evolution of North America; comparisons and contrasts between Precambrian rocks of the North American craton and Phanerozoic belts of the Cordilleran, Appalachian, Ouachita and Innuitian orogens; interrelations between sedimentation, deformation, metamorphism and magmatism in a plate tectonic context.

EOSC 333.title: Elemental and Isotopic Geochemistry
EOSC 333.description: Analytical methods in geochemistry, major and trace element geochemistry, radiogenic isotopes, geochemistry of seawater, the mantle, basalts, subduction zones, sedimentary rocks, continental crust.

EOSC 340.title: Climate Change: Causes and Solutions
EOSC 340.description: Mechanisms and processes of past and future global climate change. Climate models and projected impacts. Climate solutions including carbon sequestration, adaptation and geoengineering.
EOSC 340.prerequisiteText: Either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 120, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, CHEM_V 154 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103 and one of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 153, PHYS_V 157, PHYS_O 111

EOSC 345.title: Climate Change: Evidence and Impacts
EOSC 345.description: Climate science fundamentals: Energy balance, ocean and atmospheric circulation. Future climate scenarios. Processes driving spatial and temporal climate variability. Analysis of observations and climate projection data to evaluate the anthropogenic impact on climate.

EOSC 350.title: Environmental, Geotechnical, and Exploration Geophysics I
EOSC 350.description: Principles of geophysical survey design, data acquisition, processing and interpretation with emphasis on near-surface problems. Magnetic, seismic reflection/refraction, electromagnetic and ground penetrating radar surveys. Case history analysis of environmental and geotechnical problems.

children.raw: third-year standing or higher in Science or Applied Science

EOSC 350.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 253 and third-year standing or higher in Science or Applied Science

EOSC 352.title: Geophysical Continuum Dynamics
EOSC 352.description: Introduction to tensor calculus and continuum mechanics. Stress, strain and strain-rate tensors. Mass, momentum and energy balance. Applications to problems of geophysical heat transport, elasticity and fluid dynamics.

EOSC 353.title: Seismology
EOSC 353.description: Hooke's law for isotropic continua, elastic wave equation, reflection and refraction methods for imaging the Earth's internal structure, plane waves in an infinite medium and interaction with boundaries, body wave seismology, inversion of travel-time curves, generalized ray theory, crustal seismology, surface waves and earthquake source studies.

EOSC 354.title: Analysis of Time Series and Inverse Theory for Earth Scientists
EOSC 354.description: Continuous and discrete Fourier transforms, correlation and convolution, spectral estimates, optimum least-squares filters, deconvolution and prediction, frequency-wave number filtering. A practical course on computer techniques applied to the analysis of a wide range of geophysical phenomena.
EOSC 354.prerequisiteText: Either (a) SCIE 001 or (b) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157

EOSC 355.title: The Planets
EOSC 355.description: Diversity among the planets and moons of the solar system; integrating concepts across scientific disciplines, including geology, geophysics, and atmospheric science to understand how planets evolve.
EOSC 355.prerequisiteText: Either (a) SCIE 001 or (b) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121; and one of CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141, CHEM 154 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157

EOSC 372.title: Introductory Oceanography: Circulation and Plankton
EOSC 372.description: Physical and chemical processes and their controls on the distribution of plankton in the ocean.
EOSC 372.prerequisiteText: Either (a) SCIE 001 or (b) one of CHEM 110, CHEM 111, CHEM 120, CHEM 121, CHEM 141, CHEM 154 and one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157

EOSC 373.title: Introductory Oceanography: Climate and Ecosystems
EOSC 373.description: Physical, chemical, and biological processes in the ocean and their interaction with climate and marine food-webs.

EOSC 398.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
EOSC 398.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences.

EOSC 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
EOSC 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in Winter Session (Term 1) in third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences.

EOSC 410.title: Geoscientific Data Analysis and Empirical Modelling
EOSC 410.description: Application of data analysis and empirical modelling strategies for conducting a data-oriented research in geosciences; from setting research questions and hypothesis to delivering and interpreting results. Examples are drawn from across the Earth, ocean, atmospheric and planetary sciences.
EOSC 410.prerequisiteText: One of STAT_V 200, BIOL_V 300 and one of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 200, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, EOSC_V 250 and one of EOSC_V 211, CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210

EOSC 417.title: Stable Isotopes in Earth, Ocean, and Environmental Sciences
EOSC 417.description: Principles of stable isotope geochemistry applied to environmental systems, including instrumentation, data and sample analysis, and applications to (paleo) climate, oceanographic and environmental research.
EOSC 417.prerequisiteText: 3rd-year class standing or higher and either (a) SCIE_V 001 or (b) one of CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, CHEM_V 154 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105 or MATH_V 121

EOSC 420.title: Volcanology
EOSC 420.description: Field and lab-based studies in volcanology concentrating on physical and chemical aspects of volcanic processes.

EOSC 421.title: Advanced Sedimentology
EOSC 421.description: Description and interpretation of ancient and modern sediments, with emphasis on the origin, composition, textures, structures, diagenesis and chemistry of biogenic sediments.

EOSC 422.title: Structural Geology II
EOSC 422.description: Studies of natural deformation using advanced techniques.

EOSC 424.title: Advanced Mineral Deposits
EOSC 424.description: Advanced concepts in the processes that lead to the formation of mineral deposits. Introduction to the study of ore minerals using reflected light microscopy.

EOSC 425.title: Paleontology
EOSC 425.description: Paleobiogeography in the context of plate tectonics. Mass extinction events. Fossilization and biases in the fossil record. Species concepts in paleontology. Biostratigraphy. Paleontological evidence for early life; the colonization of oceanic and terrestrial environments and; the evolution of the primates.

EOSC 426.title: Fundamentals of Geomicrobiology
EOSC 426.description: Foundational knowledge of the interactions between microorganisms and Earth's surface chemistry. .
EOSC 426.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 111, BIOL_V 112, BIOL_V 121, CHEM_V 110, CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 120, CHEM_V 121, CHEM_V 141, EOSC_V 110, EOSC_V 112. Third year standing in Science

EOSC 428.title: Field Techniques in Groundwater Hydrology
EOSC 428.description: Hydraulic head measurements, water-quality sampling, pump and slug testing, infiltration measurements, profiling techniques. Held over five days after spring term at the Richmond groundwater hydrology field-school site. Enrolment limitations.

EOSC 429.title: Groundwater Contamination
EOSC 429.description: Contaminant transport processes in groundwater flow systems; aqueous and multiphase transport; mathematical models describing migration and chemical evolution of contaminant plumes; case studies.

EOSC 430.title: Aqueous Geochemistry
EOSC 430.description: Quantitative approaches to practical aqueous geochemistry problems. Equilibrium thermodynamics, kinetics, complexation, oxidation reduction, cation exchange, sorption and partitioning of organics. Case Studies.
EOSC 430.prerequisiteText: One of CHEM 123, CHEM 130, CHEM 154, SCIE 001

EOSC 431.title: Groundwater Remediation
EOSC 431.description: Methods for containment and remediation of subsurface contaminants; including groundwater control, groundwater extraction, and in situ treatment. Experience with common design approaches.

EOSC 432.title: Fossil Fuels
EOSC 432.description: Origin, geochemistry and distribution of petroleum and coal in the stratigraphic record. Sedimentation of organic matter, organic diagenesis, migration and accumulation of hydrocarbons. Principles of exploration and development. Techniques for measurement of organic maturation and source rock analyses.

EOSC 433.title: Geological Engineering Practice I - Rock Engineering
EOSC 433.description: Application of rock mechanics, hydrogeology, and engineering design tools in realistically complex geological environments. Influence and treatment of geological uncertainty, and use of field data, geotechnical monitoring, and numerical analyses for tunnelling, mining and rock slope engineering projects. Case histories.

EOSC 434.title: Geological Engineering Practice II - Soil Engineering
EOSC 434.description: Application of geomorphology, hydrogeology, and soil mechanics to geotechnical design. Influence and treatment of geological uncertainty in geotechnical hazard and risk assessments; multi-disciplinary approaches to geotechnical engineering problems in realistically complex geological environments. Case histories.

EOSC 440.title: Physical Climate Modelling
EOSC 440.description: Understanding climate models from 1D energy balance to fully coupled atmosphereocean general circulation models. Physics and thermodynamics of radiative balance and clouds. Spatial and temporal climate variability. Run simple climate models and analyze data from complex models.
EOSC 440.prerequisiteText: 3rd year class standing, and one of EOSC 211, EOSC 213, CPSC 203, CPSC 210, and MATH 200, and one of EOSC 112, ATSC 201, EOSC 340, EOSC 345, GEOS 102,GEOG 312, PHYS 333

EOSC 442.title: Climate Measurement and Analysis
EOSC 442.description: Local climate time series collection and analysis. Retrieval and analysis of online climate data and model output.
EOSC 442.prerequisiteText: One of EOSC 340, EOSC 345 and one of CPSC 103, CPSC 110, EOSC 211, MATH 210, PHYS 210 and one of STAT 200, STAT 201, STAT 251, BIOL 300

EOSC 445.title: Engineering Design Project
EOSC 445.description: Geological engineering design project from scope definition to final design. Based on a problem from industry. [2*-3-0, 2*-3-0]

EOSC 447.title: Thesis
EOSC 447.description: For B.A.Sc. Topic to be approved by the Department.

EOSC 448.title: Directed Studies
EOSC 448.description: Investigation of a topic to be agreed upon by a member of the faculty and the student. Permission of an undergraduate advisor and of the supervising faculty member is required before registration.

EOSC 449.title: Thesis
EOSC 449.description: Original research work under the direction of a faculty member. Required of all honours students. Open to major students with a satisfactory standing, appropriate background courses and permission of the course instructor and the directing faculty member.

EOSC 450.title: Interior Structure of Earth and Planets
EOSC 450.description: Theory, application and quantitative interpretation of potential field methods for use in exploring the interior structure of Earth and planets. Topics drawn from problems in geophysical exploration, geodesy, geodynamics, geomagnetism, planetary magnetic fields, heat flow and fluid flow.
EOSC 450.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 312, MATH 316, MATH 257 and one of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 158, SCIE 001

EOSC 453.title: Physics of the Earth and Other Planets
EOSC 453.description: Identification and quantitative analysis of diverse physical problems in the earth, ocean, atmospheric, and planetary sciences.

EOSC 454.title: Applied Geophysics
EOSC 454.description: Using geophysics to characterize the Earth's subsurface for resource exploration, engineering, or environmental applications. Data acquisition, processing, and interpretation of geophysical surveys. Inversion examples drawn from potential (electrical, magnetic, gravity) or wave field (seismic, ground penetrating radar) surveys.
EOSC 454.prerequisiteText: One of MATH_V 111, MATH_V 131, MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, and one of EOSC_V 211, CPSC_V 203, CPSC_V 210, and one of MATH_V 316, PHYS_V 312, EOSC_V 350, EOSC_V 352

EOSC 470.title: Biological Oceanography
EOSC 470.description: A quantitative examination of processes regulating the abundance, distribution and production of phytoplankton, zooplankton, microbes and fish. Controls of primary and secondary production, ecosystem dynamics and foodwebs.

EOSC 471.title: Waves, Currents and Ocean Mixing
EOSC 471.description: Use of observations, theory and model results to solve physical oceanographic problems including applications to transport and mixing of pollutants or nutrients.
EOSC 471.prerequisiteText: EOSC 211 and one of ATSC 201, EOSC 372, GEOB 200 and one of SCIE 001, PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157

EOSC 472.title: Chemical Oceanography and Marine Geochemistry
EOSC 472.description: Controls on chemical composition and elemental distributions in seawater and marine sediments (including nutrient elements, dissolved gases, the carbonate system, marine organic matter, and trace metals); solution chemistry of seawater; isotopic tracers of rates and dates in marine systems; geochemical balance in the oceans.

EOSC 473.title: Methods in Oceanography
EOSC 473.description: Methods of data acquisition, study and analysis required in solving oceanographic problems. Includes a field school held during the mid-term break. A fee is to be paid by January 31. Open to third- and fourth-year students in Oceanography, or with permission of the Department Head.

EOSC 474.title: Marine Pollution
EOSC 474.description: An interdisciplinary study of pollution, with examples drawn from coastal and oceanic environments, including areas of local interest. Intended for third and fourth-year students with a background in the sciences.

EOSC 475.title: Marine Microbiology
EOSC 475.description: Advanced biology, ecology and diversity of marine microbes. Emphasis on the roles of bacteria and viruses in marine foodwebs and geochemical cycles.

prerequisite.raw: A minimum of 6 credits of third-year level life science courses

EOSC 475.prerequisiteText: A minimum of 6 credits of third-year level life science courses

EOSC 478.title: Introduction to Fisheries Science
EOSC 478.description: An introduction to the ecology and management of freshwater and marine fisheries. Topics include: population dynamics, species interactions, communities, environmental influences, stock assessment, economics and sociology of fisheries. Laboratories will consist of numerical analyses and simulations.

EOSC 490.title: Student Directed Seminars in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences
EOSC 490.description: Self-directed, collaborative studies in earth, ocean and atmospheric sciences, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars.

EOSC 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
EOSC 498.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university of government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences.

EOSC 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
EOSC 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial, university or government setting for a minimum of 14 weeks. Normally taken in the Summer Session (Terms 1 and 2) following fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Option in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences.

EOSC 510.title: Data Analysis in Atmospheric, Earth and Ocean Sciences

EOSC 511.title: Numerical Techniques for Ocean, Atmosphere and Earth Scientists

EOSC 516.title: Teaching and Learning in Earth, Ocean and Atmospheric Sciences

EOSC 517.title: Stable Isotopes in Earth, Ocean, and Environmental Sciences
EOSC 517.description: Principles of stable isotope geochemistry applied to environmental systems, including instrumentation, data and sample analysis, and applications to (paleo) climate, oceanographic and environmental research.

EOSC 518.title: Science Communication and Outreach in Museum and Other Informal Learning Settings
EOSC 518.description: Theory and best practices for effective science communication in informal learning environments; common obstacles in communicating science to children and adults; design and rhetorical theory in the context of outreach development and communication; presentation of scientific phenomena to the public.

EOSC 519.title: Carbonate-rich Magmas and Their Mineral Deposits
EOSC 519.description: Carbonate-rich magmas—specifically carbonatites and kimberlites—as sources of iron ores, phosphates, rare earth elements, niobium, and diamonds. Origins, geological characteristics, and exploration strategies of carbonatites and kimberlites as potential hosts of economically significant mineral deposits. Open to students with appropriate background courses (ex. one of EOSC_V 321, EOSC_V 322, or a course in Igneous or/and Metamorphic Petrology with a lab component from another university).

EOSC 520.title: Advanced Mineralogy
EOSC 520.description: Crystal structure, chemistry, origin and paragenesis of major rock-forming and ore minerals.

EOSC 521.title: Microbeam and Diffraction Methods for the Characterization of Minerals and Materials

EOSC 522.title: Methods and Modelling in Petrology and Geochemistry

EOSC 525.title: Magmatic Ore Deposits
EOSC 525.description: Magmatic ore deposits and associated ore-forming systems with a focus on the petrology and geochemistry of mineralized intrusions and volcanic rocks.

EOSC 527.title: Instrumentation and Monitoring in Geological Engineering Practice
EOSC 527.description: Investigative versus performance monitoring. Monitoring requirements, limitations and system support. Tactical versus strategic monitoring. Data analysis, utilization and communication. Integration of monitoring with geotechnical and groundwater modelling. Case histories.

EOSC 528.title: Advanced Coal Geology
EOSC 528.description: The origin and character of coal and associated strata. Petrology, chemistry and physical properties of coal. Sedimentology of peat, biochemical and geochemical stages of coalification and oxidation of coal. Use of organic matter as a geothermometer and inbasinal analysis. Structural analysis and character of coal deposits. Analytical methods applied to coal.

EOSC 530.title: Advanced Igneous Petrology
EOSC 530.description: Lectures, seminars and laboratories on the application of physical chemistry to the origin of igneous rocks; crystallization processes in silicate magmas; melt physical properties, heat transfer and fluid flow.

EOSC 532.title: Field Laboratory in Groundwater Hydrology
EOSC 532.description: Hydraulic head measurements, water-quality sampling, pump and slug testing, infiltration measurements, profiling techniques. Computer analysis of field data. Held after spring term at the Richmond groundwater hydrology field site. Enrolment limitations.

EOSC 533.title: Groundwater Modelling in Practice
EOSC 533.description: Models of steady-state and transient groundwater flow in the saturated and unsaturated zones; applications to regional groundwater flow, groundwater recharge, subsurface contributions to streamflow, aquifer evaluation; model calibration. Case histories.

EOSC 534.title: Geological Engineering: Soils and Weak Rocks
EOSC 534.description: Consult the credit exclusion list in the Faculty of Science section of the Calendar.

EOSC 535.title: Transport Processes in Porous Media
EOSC 535.description: Transport of mass and heat in groundwater flow systems; modelling techniques including an introduction to the finite-element method; modelling of groundwater contamination.

EOSC 536.title: Geotechnical Modelling in Practice
EOSC 536.description: Application of geomechanics and engineering design tools in complex geological environments. Influence and treatment of geological uncertainty; use of field data, geotechnical monitoring and numerical analyses for tunnelling, mining and rock slope engineering projects. Case histories.
